errors.url_required: Enter your website address so we can look at it.
errors.url_invalid: That doesn't look like a website address. Try something like example.com.
errors.url_scheme: We can only check addresses that start with http or https.
errors.url_port: We can only check sites on the standard web ports.
errors.url_private: That address points to a private network, so we can't reach it from here.
errors.dns_failed: We couldn't find that address. Check the spelling and try again.
errors.fetch_failed: We couldn't reach that site. It may be down, or blocking us.
errors.site_error: The site answered with an error ({status}). Try the exact address you use in your browser.
errors.too_many_redirects: That address redirects in circles, so we stopped.
errors.rate_limited: That's a few checks in a short time. Wait a couple of minutes and try again.
errors.method_not_allowed: Something went wrong on our end. Try again.
errors.network: We couldn't complete the check. Try again, or email {email} with your address.
errors.not_configured: The site check isn't switched on yet. Email {email} with your address and we'll run it by hand.

https.missing.title: Your site doesn't use a secure connection
https.missing.detail: Visitors see a “not secure” warning in the address bar, and search engines rank the site lower. A certificate is free and takes minutes to install.

https.ok.title: Secure connection in place
https.ok.detail: Your site is served over HTTPS.

https.noRedirect.title: The old insecure address still works
https.noRedirect.detail: Someone typing your address without “https” stays on the insecure version. It should send them to the secure one automatically.

https.noHsts.title: The browser isn't told to always use the secure address
https.noHsts.detail: A single header (HSTS) tells browsers to never try the insecure version again. Small hardening step.

mixedContent.title: {count} things on the page still load insecurely
mixedContent.detail: Images or scripts loaded over the old insecure address can be blocked by the browser, which breaks how the page looks or works.
mixedContent.titleOne: One thing on the page still loads insecurely

wordpress.outdated.title: WordPress {version} is no longer supported
wordpress.outdated.detail: The current release is {latest}. Old versions stop getting security fixes, and most hacked sites are simply out-of-date ones. This is the first thing to deal with.

wordpress.behind.title: WordPress {version} is behind the current release
wordpress.behind.detail: The current release is {latest}. Updating is usually quick, but test it on a copy first if the site has custom code.

wordpress.versionExposed.title: Your WordPress version is visible to anyone
wordpress.versionExposed.detail: The page announces version {version} in its source. It tells an attacker exactly which weaknesses to try. Hiding it is a one-line change.

wordpress.versionUnknown.title: We couldn't read your WordPress version
wordpress.versionUnknown.detail: That's often a good sign: it means the version isn't published. Worth confirming it's current from your dashboard.

wordpress.readmeExposed.title: The WordPress readme file is public
wordpress.readmeExposed.detail: The file at /readme.html states your exact version. It serves no purpose on a live site and should be deleted.

php.eol.title: PHP {version} no longer gets security fixes
php.eol.detail: PHP is the language your site runs on. Version {version} is past its end of life; {current} is current. Your host can usually switch it in a few clicks, but plugins should be tested first.

php.securityOnly.title: PHP {version} only gets security fixes now
php.securityOnly.detail: It still receives security patches, but no more improvements. Version {current} is faster. Plan the move before support ends.

php.exposed.title: Your server announces its PHP version
php.exposed.detail: Version {version} appears in the response headers. Hiding it is a small setting change and gives attackers one less clue.

jquery.outdated.title: An old version of jQuery is loaded
jquery.outdated.detail: Version {version} is on the page; {latest} is current. Old versions have known weaknesses that scanners look for.

seo.noindex.title: Your site is telling Google not to list it
seo.noindex.detail: The page carries a “noindex” instruction. It's usually left over from building the site, and it keeps you out of search results entirely.

seo.title.missing.title: The page has no title
seo.title.missing.detail: The title is the blue line in Google results and the label on the browser tab. Without it, search engines invent one.

seo.title.long.title: The page title is long ({length} characters)
seo.title.long.detail: Google cuts titles off around 60 characters. Shorter titles keep the important words visible.

seo.title.short.title: The page title is very short ({length} characters)
seo.title.short.detail: There's room to say what you do and where, which is what people search for.

seo.description.missing.title: There's no description for search results
seo.description.missing.detail: The description is the grey text under your link in Google. Writing it yourself is free and it decides whether people click.

seo.description.long.title: The search description is long ({length} characters)
seo.description.long.detail: Google cuts it off around 155 characters, so the end may never be seen.

seo.h1.missing.title: The page has no main heading
seo.h1.missing.detail: One clear heading tells both readers and search engines what the page is about.

seo.h1.multiple.title: The page has {count} main headings
seo.h1.multiple.detail: Usually one is enough. Several competing headings muddy what the page is about.

seo.canonical.missing.title: No canonical address is set
seo.canonical.missing.detail: This tells search engines which address is the real one when a page is reachable several ways. It prevents your pages competing with each other.

seo.og.missing.title: Links to your site share badly
seo.og.missing.detail: There's no preview image or title set, so posting your link on Facebook or LinkedIn shows a bare address.

seo.schema.present.title: Search engines get structured details
seo.schema.present.detail: Your pages describe themselves in a format Google reads.

seo.schema.missing.title: No structured details for search engines
seo.schema.missing.detail: A small block of hidden data can put your address, hours, prices or reviews directly in search results.

seo.robots.missing.title: No robots.txt file
seo.robots.missing.detail: This small file tells search engines what they may look at and where your sitemap is. Most sites should have one.

seo.sitemap.present.title: A sitemap is published
seo.sitemap.present.detail: Search engines can find every page without guessing.

seo.sitemap.missing.title: No sitemap found
seo.sitemap.missing.detail: A sitemap lists your pages for search engines. Without it, newer pages can take much longer to appear.

lang.missing.title: The page doesn't declare its language
lang.missing.detail: One attribute tells browsers and screen readers which language the page is in. It also helps search engines show it to the right people.

lang.frenchMissing.title: We found no French version
lang.frenchMissing.detail: If you do business in Quebec, your site has to be available in French, at least as prominently as any other language. That's the Charter of the French Language, updated by Bill 96, not a preference.

lang.hreflangMissing.title: Your language versions aren't linked for search engines
lang.hreflangMissing.detail: There seem to be two languages, but nothing tells Google they're the same site. Each version ends up competing with the other.

lang.bilingual.title: More than one language is in place
lang.bilingual.detail: Your site declares a French version.

mobile.viewport.missing.title: The site isn't set up for phones
mobile.viewport.missing.detail: Without this one line, phones shrink the whole desktop page to fit, so the text is unreadable. Most of your visitors are on a phone.

mobile.viewport.ok.title: Set up for phones
mobile.viewport.ok.detail: The page tells phones how to display it.

speed.htmlWeight.title: The page itself is heavy ({kb} KB)
speed.htmlWeight.detail: That's just the page's own code, before images. On a phone connection it delays everything that follows.

speed.htmlWeight.info.title: The page's own code is on the large side ({kb} KB)
speed.htmlWeight.info.detail: Not a problem yet, but worth watching as you add to the site.

speed.slowResponse.title: The server took {ms} ms to answer
speed.slowResponse.detail: That's before anything is drawn on screen. Slow answers usually mean cheap hosting, no caching, or a plugin doing too much work.

speed.blockingScripts.title: {count} scripts hold up the first paint
speed.blockingScripts.detail: They load before anything appears. Marking them to load later is usually a quick win.

speed.imagesNoDimensions.title: {count} images have no size set
speed.imagesNoDimensions.detail: The page jumps around as images load, which is the thing that makes people mis-tap buttons.

speed.noLazyLoading.title: All {count} images load at once
speed.noLazyLoading.detail: Images further down the page can wait until someone scrolls to them. On a phone that saves real time and data.

a11y.imagesNoAlt.title: {count} of {total} images have no text description
a11y.imagesNoAlt.detail: Screen readers announce nothing for these, and search engines can't tell what they show. Descriptions also appear when an image fails to load.
a11y.imagesNoAlt.titleOne: 1 of {total} images has no text description

privacy.analyticsNoConsent.title: Tracking appears to run before visitors agree
privacy.analyticsNoConsent.detail: We found analytics or advertising scripts and no consent banner. In Quebec, Law 25 requires consent before tracking, with a real way to say no.

security.headers.title: {count} standard protection headers are missing
security.headers.detail: These are small server settings that block common attacks. They cost nothing and change nothing visible.

security.serverExposed.title: Your server announces its exact version
security.serverExposed.detail: The response says {server}. Hiding the version number gives attackers one less thing to work with.

items.q: Does my Quebec website need to be in French?
items.a: If you do business in Quebec, yes: your site has to be available in French, at least as prominently as any other language (the Charter of the French Language, updated by Bill 96). We build in both languages by default, and the French is written, not machine-translated.

items.q: Who owns the site when it's done?
items.a: You do — code, design, content and accounts in your name.

paragraphs: The quote tool itself collects nothing: your answers stay in your browser until you decide to send them.

When you send a quote request or a question: your name, your email address, your phone and company if you gave them, your answers to the quote questions, the range you were shown and what you wrote. Nothing else.

If you accept analytics in the banner: which pages you visit, how you got here, your device and browser type and your approximate location, through Google Analytics 4. Until you accept, no analytics script loads and no cookie is set. If you decline, nothing is collected.
Quote requests are used to prepare and confirm your quote and to follow up on it. Questions are used to answer you. Nothing else — no newsletter, no sharing, no selling.
Analytics tell us whether this site is useful and worth keeping up. That's it.

Quote requests go into Monkeys at Work's own systems: its lead database, HubSpot (the customer relationship tool) and ClickUp (the task tool), the same way a quote from the chat on monkeysat.work does. Questions go to HubSpot with a record of the consent you gave.
Analytics data goes to Google Analytics 4, with IP addresses anonymized.
Your analytics choice is remembered in your browser for 12 months. Quote requests and questions are kept for as long as we need them to follow up with you, and deleted on request.
To see, correct or delete what we hold about you, email support@monkeysat.work. We'll confirm when it's done.
To change your analytics choice, use the button below and the banner will ask again.
Monkeys at Work, Quebec, Canada. support@monkeysat.work.
